timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed serial CLI stream source with 3251 events; it was transport-only in the ledger projection.
Reviewed serial trajectory: local probing, implementation, differential fuzzer, build checks, final response, and normal closure.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the pure Rust 2021, std-only, black-box binary probing, matching CLI/output, /output Cargo project, and test4.rs requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned final implementation but delegated characterization and verification to large workflows with many probe, refute, fuzzer, judge, and audit children.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a byte-based IDNA port with a Cargo project, test4.rs entry point, library modules, tests, README, and built artifacts.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated files into the final /output artifact tree; artifact validation copied Cargo.toml, test4.rs, src/lib.rs, tests/spec.rs, README, and binaries.
parallel.verification: Ran local examples and cargo tests, and launched a broad differential verification workflow that produced concrete child findings before the parent timed out.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation passed 40/40, but the parent timed out without a normal final answer and without fully consuming the aggregate verifier workflow result.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same prompt requirements and explicitly treated the task as black-box inference from the compiled C++ binary.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept probing, implementation, build, fuzzing, and final reporting under one local owner with no child delegation.
serial.implementation: Implemented byte-count validation, byte-range ASCII/IDN checks, std-only argv handling, modular IDNA files, Cargo.toml, and test4.rs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a complete Cargo project and executable in /output with validated artifact files and no parallel workflow state.
serial.verification: Ran a 6,595-case differential fuzzer with zero mismatches, checked documented examples, cargo tests, rustc, cargo build, and dependency cleanliness.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation passed 40/40 and the agent ended normally; the only noted deviation was args_os to preserve non-UTF-8 C++ argv behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, black-box probing, /output project, test4.rs, and byte-for-byte output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same prompt requirements and explicitly documented the std-only, byte-for-byte behavior and the args_os deviation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-understanding difference drove the score; both passed the same official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run split behavior characterization and verification into large workflows while the parent retained final implementation and delivery ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept probing, implementation, fuzzing, and delivery inside one agent without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition created high coordination overhead; serial used a compact single-owner path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs included detailed common binary/port context and schemas, so the main issue was not missing task context.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained context locally and carried the inferred byte-based interface directly into implementation and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Context content was adequate in both runs; the contrast is transfer volume and timing rather than incorrect interfaces.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel artifact validation shows a complete Cargo project, test4.rs, library source, tests, and built executables in the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact validation also shows a complete Cargo project and test4.rs with modular IDNA files and built executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced accepted implementation artifacts; serial used fewer files and no workflow-produced aggregate dependency.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for the characterization workflow, timed out on retrieval, launched verification, and later waited again while workflows remained active.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced local fuzzer results directly in the main trajectory and then moved to final verification and response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel child results had a long, incomplete lifecycle; serial had immediate local result consumption.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integration resulted in a final artifact tree with Cargo files, README, tests, source, and executables; no write collision was proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integration resulted in a final artifact tree with Cargo files, test4.rs, modular idna files, and release executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both integrated successfully; parallel carried more generated artifacts and workflow state but no observed merge conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verification included local cargo tests and a broad verifier workflow that reported write-failure divergence below the parent; official evaluation still passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification included a 6,595-case differential fuzzer, documented examples, cargo tests, and build checks before normal closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was broader but not fully consumed before timeout; serial verification was narrower but completed cleanly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the 2399-second agent window and ended with returncode 143 and zero remaining budget.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial returned normally in 248.054 seconds with 2150 seconds remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process contrast: parallel budget exhaustion versus serial normal closure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current status records: both parallel and serial completed official evaluation and passed 40 of 40 tests. The concrete difference is process efficiency and closure. Parallel used broad workflows, waited repeatedly, and timed out at the agent process level after delivering a passing artifact. Serial completed the same task locally, verified with a 6,595-case fuzzer, and returned a normal final response with substantial budget remaining.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel verifier children surfaced out-of-band stdout write-failure behavior below the parent, but the official evaluator did not expose a failing testcase.
Serial documented an args_os deviation to preserve non-UTF-8 argv fidelity and did not use child workflow results.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator judged both submitted artifacts as passing 40/40, so process timeout in the parallel agent did not become an official solution failure.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized adverse parallel process consequence only

candidates.reason: The parent took implementation ownership and produced a Cargo project plus test4.rs; the issue was not absent implementation ownership.
There were no incompatible independently owned components requiring an unassigned integrator; the final tree was assembled by the parent.
The required entry file, Cargo project, tests, README, and executable artifacts were assembled and artifact validation found them present.
The parent owned the end-to-end path through probing, writing, local tests, and delivery; the adverse event was budget exhaustion, not owner absence.
Productive implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; broad probing and verification ran through parallel workflows.
The investigation was not a serial first phase; the parallel run used broad concurrent workflows and continued implementation while work remained active.
The same allocation episode is more specifically collective fan-out and repeated waits exhausting the finite run budget.

The parallel parent launched broad characterization and verification workflows, each internally fanning out into many child agents, then repeatedly blocked on workflow output. The status record shows the agent consumed the 2399-second run budget and exited 143, while the official artifact still passed. The serial run solved the same task locally with a single differential fuzzer and normal completion.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent exhausted the run budget and timed out without a normal final response or fully consumed aggregate verifier result, even though the delivered artifact later passed evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing aggregate verifier return is real, but taxonomy precedence says to absorb it when excessive verifier workflow breadth directly exhausts the finite run budget.

candidates.reason: No single child assignment is proven to be the dominant overbroad scope; the pressure came from many children and workflow breadth.
The workflow briefs included task, binary, output, and verification requirements; no known omitted child requirement produced unusable work.
No separately owned components diverged at an omitted interface contract; the final implementation was one Cargo project under parent control.
There is no before/after evidence that a known constraint disappeared through summary or compaction and caused repeated work.
The issue was not a returned handoff too large for the parent to reduce; the aggregate workflow result was not returned before timeout.
No parent decision consumed a superseded child report or obsolete workspace state.
No unresolved incompatible handoffs caused blocked or wrong integration.
The parent did not make a normal final completion decision after a visible unresolved integrated gap; official status shows evaluator completion and pass.
No replacement child or retry repeated prior work because it lacked inherited checkpoints; the workflows were broad first-pass fan-outs.

candidates.reason: There is no explicit parent stop or cancel of an active child before a needed result; the run ended by global timeout.
A complete artifact was already in the final workspace and passed official evaluation, so no promotable candidate was left unplaced.
No child implementation was merged only after the relevant verification without a follow-up check; parent tests ran after final file writes.
No completed delegated implementation was abandoned; implementation was produced by the parent in the final workspace.
A verifier finding was trapped below the aggregate workflow, but that absence is downstream of the qualifying broad fan-out budget-exhaustion episode.
No required child failure or abort left indispensable implementation scope unresumed; the artifact already existed and passed.
The parent did not have a concise completed aggregate verifier result to accept or reject; partial status visibility belongs to the same budget-exhaustion chain.
The parent checked progress and task state while waiting; the timeout wait is a downstream symptom of the broad fan-out budget episode.
No concurrent agents produced competing implementation files or behavior designs that required reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file and forcing reconciliation.
No non-entry source owned by another active agent was replaced or deleted by a concurrent writer.
No required executable or entry-point source was overwritten while another agent owned or used that deliverable.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced multiple current outputs and invalidated another actor's final-tree work.
Although the final workspace was shared, no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem was observed from concurrent writes.
No generated file, cache, helper, or fixture from one actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.

The serial run solved the same task locally with a single differential fuzzer and normal completion.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent exhausted the run budget and timed out without a normal final response or fully consumed aggregate verifier result, even though the delivered artifact later passed evaluation.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The missing aggregate verifier return is real, but taxonomy precedence says to absorb it when excessive verifier workflow breadth directly exhausts the finite run budget.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Missing Verifier Return, Blind Timeout Wait, Critical-Path Starvation, and Oversized Child Task were considered but suppressed as the same broad workflow timeout chain.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 children were considered; only the broad workflow budget episode cleared the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained label uses one episode ID, unique evidence, and one distinct consequence; downstream wait and verifier-return symptoms were not double-counted.
